proposal.reactor_type: Two-zone heated PFA coil reactor with an interstage morpholine injection tee; Zone 1 is the oxidation hold-up coil and Zone 2 is the oxidative amidation hold-up coil.
proposal.residence_time_basis: Substrate-molecule residence time. Zone 1 is 5.0 mL at 0.500 mL/min (10.0 min before morpholine addition); Zone 2 is 12.0 mL at 0.600 mL/min (20.0 min after morpholine addition). Total molecular residence time is therefore 30.0 min. The reactor volume is 17.0 mL, not 18.0 mL, because the flow increases at the interstage injection point.
proposal.light_setup: None; operate as a thermally driven flow process.

streams.contents: Sodium bromide, 0.200 M, and sulfuric acid, 0.200 M
streams.solvent: Dioxane/water, approximately 4:1 v/v; prepare as a homogeneous solution if possible

streams.contents: tert-Butyl hydroperoxide, 6.00 M, freshly diluted from commercial aqueous TBHP immediately before use
streams.solvent: Dioxane/water, selected to maintain a single pumpable liquid phase

proposal.mixer_type: Three sequential corrosion-resistant static mixers or low-dead-volume PFA T-mixers: A+B, then +C, followed after Zone 1 by +D.
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Benzyl alcohol is first combined with NaBr/H2SO4, then TBHP is introduced immediately before the oxidation coil to minimize peroxide residence in a strongly acidic bromide-containing premix. Morpholine is injected only after the 10 min oxidation zone so that the alcohol-to-aldehyde oxidation is given an opportunity to proceed before amide formation. This also avoids storing or premixing morpholine with acidic TBHP.
pre_reactor_steps: Charge separate, labeled feed reservoirs; do not premix TBHP with sulfuric acid, NaBr, or morpholine in a reservoir.
Use a cooled and vented TBHP reservoir, preferably maintained below 25 C and protected from contamination by metals, amines, and reducing agents.
Prepare Stream B only after confirming NaBr dissolution; if solids persist, reduce NaBr concentration or increase the water fraction while maintaining the specified molar feed rate.
Prime the system with dioxane, pressure-test with solvent, and establish 5.0 bar back-pressure before introducing oxidant.
Start Streams A, B, and D first with C replaced by solvent; confirm stable flow and absence of leaks. Introduce Stream C last and allow at least two total reactor residence times before sampling.
post_reactor_steps: Pass the hot outlet through the 5 bar back-pressure regulator before any quench operation.
Cool the depressurized outlet to below 25 C in a heat exchanger.
Quench residual peroxide first with an aqueous sodium thiosulfate stream under controlled addition and external cooling; use peroxide test strips to verify destruction.
After peroxide destruction, neutralize carefully with aqueous sodium bicarbonate or dilute sodium carbonate in a vented mixer/separator. Do not acid/base-quench before confirming peroxide removal.

Separate aqueous and organic phases, wash the organic phase with brine, dry, remove solvent, and assay crude product by HPLC or quantitative NMR. Purify by flash chromatography or crystallization as required.
chemistry_notes: The reported batch protocol does not specify TBHP loading, NaBr loading, sulfuric-acid loading, TBHP assay, water content, or the individual time allocated to oxidation versus amidation. The 3.0 equiv TBHP, 0.10 equiv NaBr, 0.10 equiv H2SO4, and 10 min plus 20 min zoning are explicit translation assumptions and require optimization.

At the combined reactor outlet, benzyl alcohol and morpholine are each nominally 0.667 M: 0.400 mmol/min divided by 0.600 mL/min. This preserves the stated 0.667 M reaction concentration interpretation for each coupling partner.

The process contains water from commercial TBHP and the promoter stream. Product yield and selectivity may be sensitive to water content, TBHP concentration, acid loading, and the extent of aldehyde accumulation in Zone 1.

The expected transformation is oxidative conversion of benzyl alcohol to a benzoyl-morpholine product under bromide/acid/TBHP conditions. Monitor for benzaldehyde, benzoic acid, benzyl bromide, and morpholine oxidation byproducts.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Set equal to the reported total 30 min batch hold time as a first-pass residence-time target.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: The final reactor flow is 0.600 mL/min after morpholine injection; Zone 1 has a lower flow of 0.500 mL/min.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Set to the reported batch temperature of 80 C.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Defined as the final in-reactor concentration of each 1:1 coupling partner, benzyl alcohol and morpholine, rather than the concentration in an individual stock solution.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: A 5 bar back-pressure regulator provides liquid-phase control and suppresses bubble formation at 80 C while remaining a moderate pressure for peroxide service.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: A two-zone design implements the stated two-step sequence without requiring isolation of an intermediate aldehyde.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA is selected for compatibility with dilute sulfuric acid, bromide salt solutions, dioxane, and TBHP while avoiding metal contact with peroxide.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: A 1.0 mm ID coil provides practical heat transfer and mixing at the stated flow rates; approximately 21.6 m total tubing gives 17.0 mL internal volume.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Calculated from 5.0 mL oxidation hold-up plus 12.0 mL post-morpholine hold-up.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: No photochemical component was described in the batch protocol.
reasoning_per_field.streams: Concentrated feeds are used so that the combined reaction mixture reaches 0.667 M in both benzyl alcohol and morpholine despite addition of promoter and oxidant streams.
reasoning_per_field.mixing_order_reasoning: Segregation reduces the risk of prolonged contact between concentrated TBHP and acid, bromide, or amine before controlled reactor entry.
reasoning_per_field.post_reactor_steps: Peroxide destruction is placed before neutralization because quenching acidic oxidizing mixtures with bicarbonate can cause uncontrolled gas evolution and heat release.
reasoning_per_field.safety_flags: TBHP, acid, bromide, elevated temperature, and dioxane require conservative operating limits, compatible materials, shielding, and a validated quench.

literature_analogies: This design follows general continuous-flow oxidation practice: meter organic substrate and oxidant separately, minimize oxidant inventory, use a heated small-volume reactor, and employ back-pressure control.

The delayed-amine-addition arrangement is a process-development analogy for tandem alcohol oxidation/amide-forming sequences where accumulation of the carbonyl intermediate is undesirable or where direct premixing of amine with oxidant is unsafe.
No exact literature-validated continuous-flow precedent for this specific NaBr/H2SO4/TBHP benzyl alcohol-to-benzoyl morpholine system is claimed here.
safety_flags: TBHP is a strong organic peroxide oxidant; assess the exact commercial concentration, stabilizers, decomposition temperature, and maximum allowable inventory before operation.
Do not store or premix TBHP with sulfuric acid, NaBr, morpholine, transition-metal contamination, or reducing agents.
Use peroxide-compatible pumps and wetted parts; avoid copper, brass, mild steel, and unknown elastomers in contact with TBHP.

Operate behind a blast shield or in an appropriately rated ventilated enclosure with remote pump control, pressure relief, temperature interlock, and a high-pressure shutdown set below the weakest-component rating.
Install a pressure sensor upstream of the BPR, a thermocouple at each heated zone, and an automated shutdown that stops heating and oxidant feed on overtemperature, overpressure, or loss of flow.
Keep the TBHP feed reservoir cooled and low inventory; prepare only the amount needed for the experiment.
Dioxane is flammable and peroxide-forming on storage; use fresh, inhibitor-managed solvent and avoid ignition sources.
Sodium bicarbonate neutralization can evolve carbon dioxide; perform it downstream of the BPR in a vented, cooled apparatus.
Start at reduced scale, for example 0.1 to 0.2 of the stated flow rates, while retaining residence time, and establish mass balance and peroxide quench performance before extended operation.

confidence.basis: The hydraulic design, concentration calculation, and staged residence-time calculation are internally consistent. Chemical confidence is limited because critical reagent loadings and the detailed batch sequence were not provided.
recommended_validation: Run a short residence-time/temperature screen around 20 to 40 min total residence time and 70 to 90 C.
Screen TBHP from 2 to 4 equiv and NaBr/H2SO4 from 0.05 to 0.20 equiv each.
Measure peroxide conversion, benzaldehyde accumulation, benzoic-acid formation, and benzoyl morpholine yield by HPLC or GC with an internal standard.
Confirm that Stream B remains homogeneous and that no salt deposition occurs during at least 2 hours of operation.
